module_description: Module 22 covers understanding who the audience is: inference of demographics (age, gender, location) from text and profiles, audience overlap and reach/dedup measurement, media-mix/cross-platform attribution, and consent-based first-party measurement as the 2026 norm. Students build an audience profile for a topic/brand and learn the uncertainty of inferred versus declared attributes.
core_concepts: Inferred vs declared attributes and their uncertainty
First-party consented data as the 2026 standard
learning_outcomes: C3 Build an audience profile with uncertainty estimates
C4 Explain reach/dedup measurement across platforms
C5 Evaluate fake-audience risk for a creator/brand
methods_models: Text-based attribute inference (name, bio, language, location cues), probabilistic age/gender models, overlap estimation (survey or model-based), fake-follower scoring
evaluation_metrics: Accuracy of inference vs ground truth, confidence intervals on reach, overlap metric agreement, calibration of inferred probabilities
pitfalls_limitations: Inference errors by group, bias amplification, over-claiming reach numbers, consent limits on profiling, privacy law constraints on sensitive inferences
tools_stack: scikit-learn/transformers for inference, geonames, census/IPS data for calibration
commercial_platforms: Commercial audience-insights tools (Pulsar, Talkwalker audience modules) for comparison
tools_access_cost: Audience tools are usually licensed; inference from public data is free but legally sensitive
lab_activities: Build an audience profile for a topic (language mix, location mix, inferred interests) with caveats
datasets_apis: Public topic corpora + declared demographics where available
assessment_methods: Lab submission plus a short strategy recommendation memo; graded on metric validity and quality of reasoning
data_collection_workflow: Collect short-video metadata and media -> transcribe/OCR -> extract retention and engagement features -> normalise by follower base -> analyse and report
textbooks: Measurement literature on cross-platform reach and first-party data (industry reports 2025-2026)
key_papers: Hootsuite/We Are Social 2026 trends on consent-based first-party data
Papers on audience measurement and deduplication
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: measurement shifted to consent-based first-party data; 'chaos culture' and community-based content changed what an audience even means
industry_relevance: Directly used in short-form content strategy, creator-marketing measurement, and social-commerce analytics teams; the metrics in this module (watch time, completion, saves, CTR via video) are the same KPIs agencies report to clients.
localization_context: Taught against the Indonesian short-video and live-commerce ecosystem (TikTok Shop, live shopping sessions, Shopee/Tokopedia live), which has different content formats and monetization mechanics from the US market.
ethics_regulation: Disclosure of paid partnerships, sponsored content and affiliate links; UU PDP and platform rules on scraping engagement data; caution when profiling creators and audiences from public metrics.
case_study_scenarios: Profile the audience of a TikTok campaign and estimate reach with confidence intervals.
